changelog.d35d794c003e: The realistic hands. A pair of hands now plays the piano on Handscore's stage the way a pianist would — each finger chosen for the passage, the thumb passing under on a scale, a hand lifting up and over the other when the music crosses. Sixty-two public-domain classics are ready to learn, from Mary Had a Little Lamb to Silent Night and The Star-Spangled Banner, and a transport under the stage lets you pause, rewind, fast-forward or drag to any moment, hearing the notes as you go.
changelog.0390e4a43a0a: **Realistic hands at the keyboard.** Two hands, ending at the wrist, play every note on all four pianos: each finger chosen as a pianist would choose it, the thumb passing under on scales, wide chords reached, the thumb lying on its side and gently bent, and a hand lifting up and over the other to cross. They rest on the keys, ready, when nothing plays.
changelog.2c009dbabcfe: **Fingering worked out before a note sounds.** Handscore decides which hand plays each note and with which finger before the music plays, so the hands arrive as the keys go down rather than after.
changelog.216f61cb53a3: **Select Mode.** The button at the top left (or P) now reads *Select Mode* and opens your choices by category: Instruments, Classics, Passages, and Lessons (coming in a later version).
changelog.44952a5f65fd: **Sixty-two classics to learn.** Nursery songs, Christmas songs and carols, folk songs, spirituals and anthems, classical themes and piano favourites — Chopsticks, Jingle Bells, Silent Night, Ode to Joy, Für Elise, The Entertainer, The Star-Spangled Banner and more — each arranged for two hands, the melody in the right and the chords in the left. Search them by title or composer. Every one is in the public domain.
changelog.d8fc29c977d3: **Passages to watch.** A scale, a ii–V–I, an arpeggio and a crossing, each a quick look at the hands at work.
changelog.d0ff9a5e5f3f: **The transport.** Play, pause, stop, rewind and fast-forward under the stage, with a timeline showing the song's time and its bars. Hover over the timeline to see the hands at that moment in a small preview. Drag along it, or hold rewind or fast-forward, and you hear every note you pass, in either direction.
changelog.197a823169eb: **A metronome.** Switch it on and a click marks each beat, the first of every bar higher, while the dots beside its *M* show the beat.
changelog.dd397e7c80b2: **The instrument button is now Select Mode**, and the piano you choose is marked *Current* among the Instruments.
changelog.14c84d5c455f: The real pianos. Four pianos now stand on Handscore's stage — a concert grand, a parlor grand, a studio upright and an old saloon upright — each lit like a studio and each with its own voice. Click a key or play from your DAW and the piano plays: the key goes down, its name fades, and the sustain pedal holds what you let go. A picker lets you hear a piano before you choose it.
changelog.a8f76e859570: **Four real pianos.** Grand Piano, Acoustic Piano, Upright Piano and Honky-Tonk Piano, each with its own shape, finish and sound, in both themes.
changelog.6f544a8bd67f: **Play the keys.** Click a key to hear it, or slide across the keys to play each in turn. MIDI from your DAW plays the piano and moves its keys, and the sustain pedal holds the notes you let go until you lift it.
changelog.3f265130a08f: **Keys that move like a piano's.** Each key goes down on its balance rail, faster the harder it is played, and its name fades while it is down and comes back when it rises.
changelog.7fd2c1ed940d: **The piano picker.** The instrument button at the top left (or P) opens four cards. *Preview* plays a short phrase on that piano without switching; *Choose* puts it on the stage, crossfading from the last one. Your choice is saved with your project.
changelog.72aa386a33ff: **Quality that fits your computer.** Handscore measures how fast your computer draws the stage and settles on the quality it can hold smoothly.
changelog.58e041aeca75: **Keys keep up on a busy computer.** A key played while the computer was slow to draw could stay up, or its name stay half-faded; it now always ends where your playing left it.
changelog.ff94e0b1d59f: The foundation. Freally Handscore loads as a CLAP and VST3 plugin and as a standalone app, asks you to accept its licence, and opens on its stage: an 88-key keyboard at a real piano's measurements, with every key named on its front. Nothing is generated yet — that arrives with the real pianos and the hands.
changelog.37cee751dc57: **The plugin and the standalone app.** CLAP and VST3 on Windows (the AU is built on a Mac), and a standalone app that wears Handscore's icon in its title bar and taskbar.
changelog.bf0d03d43bfd: **The licence agreement comes first.** Until you agree, Handscore does nothing. Your answer is kept on your computer and shared by every open copy, in every DAW and in the standalone app.
changelog.28bc52fb055e: **The stage.** An 88-key keyboard, A0 to C8, at a real piano's measurements, filling the width of the window. Every key's name is on its front — white keys in dark ink, black keys in white — and hides while the key is down.
changelog.d51fdbedfc0e: **Light and dark.** The switch at the top right; Handscore remembers your choice.
changelog.9e0609310c1a: **Eighteen languages.** Handscore starts in your system's language.
changelog.f1cf7c9dfaa8: **A 3D view that says when it cannot draw.** A window without WebGL 2 explains how to turn it on instead of showing nothing.
changelog.0fe089d138d3: **Crashes are kept, never sent.** If Handscore ever stops unexpectedly, a short report is kept on your computer for the next launch. Nothing leaves your computer unless you choose to report it.
